text:
alex.cheung: Heads up — I'm drafting a deployment policy for the precision sweep (FP8 / INT8 / AWQ / GPTQ) we discussed. Goal: safe, measurable bring-up across hosted, dedicated, and private. High level: staged gates, traffic split by profile, automatic rollback/fallback on quality regressions. looking for feedback.

maya.kapoor: Love the approach. Can we make the gating decision depend on both latency and a holdout eval on our regression set? not just token-latency.

samuel.park: +1. Also include a percentage-based quality delta threshold (e.g., -0.8% top-1 on our LMQA set) before we trigger rollback.

alex.cheung: Yep — plan is: 1) smoke deploy to 1 host in dedicated/private or 0.1% traffic in hosted 2) run live evals against prompt set + synthetic stress 3) if quality within delta and p50/p95 latency within SLO, expand to 5%/single pool 4) final ramp to steady-state with cache/quant-profiles enabled.

jen.murphy: How do we handle mixed routing when a quant variant fails? e.g., AWQ fails quality but INT8 OK. Do we route traffic by model tag?

liam.ng: We should have hierarchical routing: route by (customer tier -> region -> model-tag). If a quant tag fails, route that traffic to the next compatible variant and mark the failing variant as quarantined for that deployment ID.

alex.cheung: Exactly. Proposed policy snippet:

```
# deploy_policy: precision_sweep_v1
stages:
  - gate: smoke
    traffic: 0.1%
    checks:
      - eval: holdout_lmqa
        max_delta_pct: -0.8
      - latency_p95_ms: 300
  - gate: pool_expand
    traffic: 5%
    checks:
      - eval: holdout_lmqa
        max_delta_pct: -0.4
      - latency_p95_ms: 350
  - gate: ramp
    traffic: 100%
    checks:
      - dynamic_monitoring: true
fallbacks:
  - on_quality_failure: route_to: compatible_variant
  - on_latency_failure: route_to: lower_throughput_variant
quarantine_ttl: 24h
```

samuel.park: That looks good. One addition: include a "verification window" after each stage where we sample outputs and run automated evals with a higher weight on failure cases. Maybe 15 minutes for smoke, 2 hours for pool_expand.

maya.kapoor: Also need rules for private deployments: many customers will opt out of live evals (data residency). For private, require local eval artifacts (customer-provided prompts + offline metrics) before stage promotion.

jen.murphy: Ops note: alerts need to be noisy for the first 24h and then relax. We should create a synthetic request generator tied to the rollout to produce consistent traffic for latency and cache warmup. ops-bot will kick off the generator.

ops-bot: Scheduled synthetic traffic job: precision-sweep-1718123456 started for 30m. Logs -> https://ci.redwood/precision-sweep/1718123456

liam.ng: For observability, capture token-level cost delta and inference GPU utilization per variant. We had a case where AWQ saved cost but increased p95 for long context. Want to detect that automatically.

alex.cheung: Good call. We'll add metrics: cost_per_1k_tokens, p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, sample_quality_score. These will be part of the gating checks.

samuel.park: One more: fallback ordering table. e.g., fallback preference for hosted: FP8_fast -> INT8_balanced -> AWQ_cost -> gptq_maxquality. For dedicated/private, prefer variants that match customer's quant support and certs.

alex.cheung: Agreed. I'll update the policy and open a short RFC with examples and a small test harness. Plan: run internal sweep next week on a dev pool and share result dashboard. Anyone want to co-own the smoke harness?

maya.kapoor: I can pair on the eval harness and assemble the holdout sets.

jen.murphy: I'll own the synthetic traffic and alerting config.

liam.ng: I'll add the cost/counters into the console dashboards.

alex.cheung: Great — I'll publish RFC today and tag you all. Thanks! :rocket:
